Ah Ma, your grandson {grandname} is speaking. Something bad happened this morning.
grandchild1_3: Ah Ma, I need the money within the hour or they will not let me go home.

grandchild1_4: How is your knee, Ah Ma? Sorry I did not come by last Sunday.

grandchild1_5: Please do not tell Papa and Mama. I cannot face them if they find out.
Ah Ma, keep this between us only. If the family hears about it, I am finished.
Do not say anything to anyone at home. Not Uncle, not my sister, nobody.
grandchild1_6: I am at the {place} office now, sitting outside the room.
They say the paperwork takes about two hours to finish.
I will be here the whole morning. Nobody is letting me walk out yet.
grandchild1_7: Do not call my handphone, Ah Ma. They took it from me, this is a borrowed line.
You cannot ring me back on this number. Just stay on the phone with me now.
Please do not check with Papa first. By the time he picks up, it is already too late for me.
bank1_1: Good morning. Am I speaking to the account holder, please?
Hello, thank you for picking up. This is the Merlion Bank fraud desk.
Good afternoon. Sorry to trouble you, this call is about your account.
bank1_2: This is officer {officer} from the Merlion Bank fraud team.
Merlion Bank fraud desk here, officer {officer} speaking.
My colleague passed me your file just now. Officer {officer} from Merlion Bank, at your service.
bank1_3: We have about eleven minutes before the payment leaves your account for good.
Please stay with me. If we stop now, the money is gone and I cannot pull it back.
The system is counting down on my screen, so please answer quickly, one question at a time.
bank1_4: I know this is a lot to take in before breakfast. Take a breath first.
Yes, the line is a bit noisy. The office here is always like that.
You are not the first person to be surprised today. It has been a busy morning.
bank1_5: Read me the sixteen numbers on the front of your card, slowly.
I need your full name, your identity card number, and the three digits printed behind the card.
What is the password you use for the app? I have to match it against our record.
bank1_6: Please write down case reference {ref} on a piece of paper.
Our office hours are nine to six, Monday to Friday.
I will note this call in your file under badge {badge} later today.
bank1_7: Move everything into the holding account I am about to read out. It is a safe account.
Transfer the balance now, {amount} or whatever is inside, into our protection account.
Withdraw the cash and hand it to our courier at your door. That is the fastest way to keep it safe.
parcel1_1: Good morning. ParcelGo calling about a package under your name.
Hello, sorry to disturb. This is ParcelGo delivery support.
Good day. Am I speaking with the person who lives at this address?
parcel1_2: This is {officer} from the ParcelGo customs desk.
ParcelGo customs clearance here, officer {officer} speaking.
My name is on your delivery note. Officer {officer}, ParcelGo customs.
parcel1_3: There is a {item} parcel waiting at our {place} sorting centre.
It came in on Tuesday night and has been at the {place} centre since then.
The box is small, about the size of a shoebox. Delivery was attempted once already.
parcel1_4: Before I release it, give me your full name and your identity card number.
I need the last four digits of your bank card to match the delivery record.
Tell me your date of birth and your home address, exactly as it is written.
parcel1_5: Aiyo, the queue at our counter today is very long. Sorry to keep you waiting.
Yes, the parcel was sent from overseas. It happens a lot around this time of year.
Take your time. I can hear the television, please turn it down a little.
parcel1_6: The customs charge is small, {amount} only. Buy shopping vouchers and read me the codes.
Go to the shop downstairs, buy gift cards, then scratch them and read me the numbers.
We cannot take cash or a normal transfer. Vouchers are the only way to clear this parcel.
parcel1_7: Our hotline is down for maintenance today, so please do not put the phone down.
Do not call the number on our website, nobody will pick up. Settle it with me now.
Please stay on the line. If you check with somebody else, the parcel goes back overseas tonight.
affirm_catch: Good ear. That one is a classic.
Yes lah, that line is the giveaway.
Nice catch. A real caller would not push like that.
That is exactly the bit to watch for.
benign_greeting: A hello is just a hello. Real callers open the same way, so this line on its own tells you nothing.
Nothing wrong with a greeting. Even the clinic starts a call like this.
That is only the opening. Keep listening, the tells usually come later.
Good to be careful. A polite hello is not proof either way, so hold it lightly.
benign_identity: Callers do introduce themselves. A name and a title alone are not proof, and not a red flag either.
Real staff say who they are too. The question is what they ask for next.
Anyone can say a name out loud. Watch what comes after the introduction.
Introductions are ordinary. Nothing here to act on yet.
benign_smalltalk: Small talk happens on real calls too. Warmth by itself is not a warning sign.
A bit of chit chat is ordinary. Scammers use it, so do your neighbours.
That was just friendly noise. Nothing to act on, nothing to worry about.
People fill the silence. It costs you nothing to listen through it.
benign_logistics: Times, places and reference numbers turn up on real calls constantly. This one is ordinary.
Details like this sound official because ordinary calls have them too. Not a tell on its own.
A case number is easy to invent and also easy to have for real. It sits in the middle.
Practical arrangements are normal. Pressure is the thing you are listening for.
recap_urgency: Real staff let you hang up and think. Anyone who insists it must happen this minute is stopping you from checking.
Hurry is the whole trick. Fear makes people skip the one phone call that would have saved them.
A genuine problem is still there in an hour. A countdown on the phone is a pressure tactic.
When somebody rushes you, that is your cue to slow down instead.
recap_secrecy: No honest caller needs you to hide the call from your own family. Secrecy keeps your helpers away.
The moment you are told not to tell anyone, tell someone. That is the whole defence.
Real offices expect you to talk it over at home. Only a scam needs silence.
Secrecy is a tool, not shame. It leaves you alone with the person who is lying to you.
recap_unusual_payment: Vouchers, gift cards and cash handed to a courier cannot be traced or reversed. That is exactly why they ask for them.
No real office collects a fee in shopping codes. That request alone can end the call.
A safe account you never opened is not safe. Money that moves there does not come back.
Watch how they want to be paid. An odd payment method is the clearest sign of all.
recap_no_callback: Blocking you from ringing back is the tell. A real office is happy for you to call the number you already have.
Anyone who cannot let you hang up and verify is hiding from that check.
You can always put the phone down and call the number printed on your own card or letter.
A dead hotline and a borrowed phone are excuses. Both exist to keep you on this call.
recap_detail_fishing: Nobody legitimate asks for your full card number, your password, or the digits behind the card. They already hold what they need.
Your details are the prize. Once they have them, they no longer need your permission for anything.
Real staff verify you, they do not collect you. Being asked to read out everything is backwards.
If a caller is building a form out of your life, stop answering and put the phone down.
shield_earned: One more shield on the wall. That is practice, not luck.
Shield earned. You will hear that voice coming next time.
Well done today. Come back tomorrow and the ear gets sharper.
That is a shield. Keep them stacking up.
Another one for the collection. Steady.
walkthrough_intro: Let us slow down and see what would have happened next.
No harm done, this is only practice. Let us walk through it together.
That is how it catches people, and it catches sharp people too. Have a look at what was really going on.
Alright, let us rewind and look at that call properly.
